closing: Tafsīr is how the Qur'ān stops being words you pass over.

captions.en: The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, now mentions tafsīr.
Tafsīr, linguistically, comes from al-fasr — which means what?
It is the uncovering of what is covered.
To remove the veil from something — to make it clear, open and apparent.

captions.ar: وَفِي الِاصْطِلَاحِ: بَيَانُ مَعَانِي الْقُرْآنِ الْكَرِيمِ
captions.en: And in terminology: clarifying the meanings of the Noble Qur'ān.
It is to clarify the meaning of the Qur'ān.
That is what the word tafsīr means.
Learning tafsīr is wājib — as Allah, the Most High, said:

captions.ar: كِتَابٌ أَنْزَلْنَاهُ إِلَيْكَ مُبَارَكٌ لِيَدَّبَّرُوا آيَاتِهِ وَلِيَتَذَكَّرَ أُولُو الْأَلْبَابِ
captions.en: “A blessed Book We have sent down to you, that they may ponder its verses, and that those of understanding may remember.”
We sent this Book down, mubārak — full of barakah. Why did We send it down?
That they may ponder its verses —
and that those of understanding may remember.
